newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds edge up, slow market seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds edge up, slow market seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late morning Monday in slow, quiet activity.
Traders said the market was up on a small bout of early short-covering but the lack of flows in the market had traders saying the price action had little significance.
"Sincerely, I do not expect much to happen in the market this week," said a trader at a local bank. "There is not much to comment."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was flat at 89-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.23 to 125.55.
Another trader said "there is very little happening."
Players noted there could be some moderate gains during the week in the absence of any key U.S. economic indicators, giving the market an opportunity not to be hampered by U.S. inflation worries.
But the U.S. sale of two- and five-year bonds during the week could weigh on Argentine bonds if U.S. Treasuries suffer from the new supply.
